questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nice city and interesting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, but the courses came out very late. Difficult if you need to choose courses yourself but okay if you take a minor

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The incoming exchange office was hopeless. They did not know anythinh about what to do. They blamed it on the leader being on vacation, but they could never answer my questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Two different kinds of dorms and also shared appartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A kitchen was available with pans and pots. There was no oven and the equipment was doubtful but in the end it all worked out fine

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It’s very fun living on campus. Almost all international students on the university live there. Also way easier and cheaper than finding something yourself

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was part of a minor were you had to write an application, so I just wrote that and then they did the rest

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn’t go through much registration due to my chosen minor

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, they fixed everything

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be well prepared and have lots of plan B’s if you’re not choosing a minor as no overlaps between classes are allowed

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Reminded me off home, maybe a bit easier as they almost only have multiple choice and therefore don’t need to go as much in depth

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more class time and it was mostly lectures. Very little individual work and no theoretical classes working with the knowledge gained. They also had mandatory attendance and no books at all

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cancer Immunity and Personalized Therapies and bachelor thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The bachelor thesis was very good for learning how to write a systematic review. Also did enjoy the autoimmunity part of the cancer courses

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, the meat was way more expensive than I thougt it would be

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Chicken was hella expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a sports center were you could do a lot of different sports. Generally they do also have a lot of not uni affliated sports clubs you can join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of a local football team called AMVJ. It was very fun, with both practices and a weekly game would definetly recommend. You can just text the club saying you’re and international student and want to talk to Kabir, then you'll be part of a very fun group of guys

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of very cute bars in areas like De Pijp and Jordaan. Go to bars such as cafe thijssen and cafe gollem for cheap and good beers.
If you’re into raving and in general edm culture there is a lot of good clubs and a whole event called AFE which you should look into

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, not very different from Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everybody is there to have fun and meet new people, just go out there and be yourself. With time you’ll find your people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking culture and the walkable city

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live at the campus dorm for having the most fun
Go out and enjoy the city and all the things to do as often as possible, you can always read in the exam period
Be open and meet as many people as possible, they all want the same as you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rent a bike at swapfiets

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world. We had 6 different continents just between the 14 people on my floor

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to balance having fun and passing exams:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
